hyg-v41: Positions, apparent magnitudes, and B−V colors for the real nearby-star field in /explore's Stellar Neighborhood. Merges the Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star, and Gliese catalogues.
d3-celestial-constellations: The modern IAU constellation stick-figures, drawn in /explore's stellar neighborhood and in each named star's finder chart. Star positions are our own (from HYG); this provides the line pattern.
gcat: Agency-grade launch log used as the trunk source for the launches calendar — dates, vehicles, and payload records for historical and current spaceflights.
ll2-thespacedevs: Upcoming-launch gap-fill aggregator for the launches calendar, used where agency-direct sources do not yet cover a launch. A leaf source, not the trunk (PRD-020).
nasa-exoplanet-archive: Confirmed exoplanet orbital elements (period, semi-major axis, eccentricity), radii, masses, and discovery metadata for the host stars rendered as BodyScene mini-orreries in /explore’s Stellar Neighborhood.
openngc: Positions (RA/Dec J2000), object types, magnitudes, and common names for the Messier catalogue plus the NGC/IC objects rendered as deep-sky billboards and labelled dots in /explore’s Known Universe. A dozen famous non-catalogue objects (Cartwheel, Tycho's SNR, the Horsehead, Cassiopeia A) carry explicit standard J2000 positions.
gravity-eht-galactic-centre: Real astrometry underpinning /explore’s Milky Way schematic: the Sun's distance to the Galactic Centre (R₀ ≈ 8.18 kpc, GRAVITY Collaboration 2019) and the mass of Sagittarius A* (≈ 4.3 million solar masses, GRAVITY Collaboration 2022; imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope 2022). The Galaxy's spiral positions are schematic; these facts are cited and real.
black-hole-parameters: Cited parameters for /explore’s geodesic gravitational-lensing renders: M87* (first imaged, EHT 2019), Sagittarius A* (EHT 2022; GRAVITY mass), and Cygnus X-1 (stellar-mass, mass revised upward by Miller-Jones et al. 2021). Gargantua is labelled fiction (Kip Thorne's Interstellar model). The lensing image is our own geodesic ray-trace — no observatory imagery is embedded.
celestrak: Two-line element sets for the ISS (NORAD 25544) and Tiangong (48274), refreshed daily and cached, that drive the Physics Lab's satellite-pass prediction (when the station next flies over you, how high, from which bearing).
jpl-iau-constants: The authoritative constants the Physics Lab kernel computes from: JPL's Keplerian elements for approximate planetary positions (Standish), IAU gravitational parameters and precession series, the EGM96 geopotential constant, and IUGG mean radii. The Lab's numbers are ours; these reference values are cited and real.
models-ref-wikipedia: Wikipedia articles (English, Russian and Chinese) that gave the lengths, diameters and proportions of the launcher and spacecraft models and the heights of the landmarks, statues and animals drawn beside them in the /fleet line-ups. The models and outlines are our own; only measurements were read.
models-ref-nssdca: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) spacecraft and launch-vehicle pages that gave the masses, lengths and diameters of the craft and rockets modelled for /fly and the /fleet line-ups.
models-ref-nasa: NASA mission, vehicle and history pages (nasa.gov, history.nasa.gov, science.nasa.gov) that gave the dimensions of the crewed capsules, cargo craft, Shuttle orbiters and launchers modelled for /fly and the /fleet line-ups.
models-ref-nps: The National Park Service “Statue Statistics” page for the Statue of Liberty: its 92.99 m height from the ground to the torch tip, with the pedestal and the statue itself — the scale figure beside the rockets in the /fleet launcher line-up.
models-ref-esa: European Space Agency pages (ATV, Ariane, Rosetta and others) that gave the dimensions of the European craft and launchers modelled for /fly and the /fleet line-ups.
models-ref-jaxa: JAXA pages on the H-IIA, H3, M-V and the HTV / HTV-X transfer vehicles that gave the dimensions of the Japanese launchers and cargo craft modelled for /fly and the /fleet line-ups.
models-ref-isro: ISRO launcher and Gaganyaan pages (PSLV, GSLV Mk III / LVM3, the crew module) that gave the dimensions of the Indian vehicles modelled for /fly and the /fleet line-ups.
models-ref-agencies: Official pages of space agencies and manufacturers (Roscosmos, SpaceX, United Launch Alliance, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, Firefly, Arianespace, the China Manned Space Agency and CASC, the U.S. Space Force) that gave vehicle dimensions for the launcher and spacecraft models.
models-ref-independent: Independent spaceflight references and museum pages (Gunter’s Space Page, Encyclopedia Astronautica, RussianSpaceWeb, the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, the Technik Museum Speyer and others) that gave the sizes of the Soviet, Shuttle and Buran-era vehicles.
nasa-mmgis-rover-traverses: The rover teams' localized drive paths for Curiosity and Perseverance, drawn on the Mars surface view with their sols and distances.
pds-mer-traverses: The science teams' localized drive paths for Spirit and Opportunity, drawn on the Mars surface view with their sols and distances.
